patterns.usage_note: A noun meaning 'intention', so it takes the dictionary form and a copula: 〜つもりだ. It reports a plan already formed and held, which is why it sounds settled next to the on-the-spot 〜(よ)う, and why asking a superior 何をするつもりですか can come out accusatory. The negative 〜ないつもりだ says the plan is not to act; 〜つもりはない denies having any such intention at all.

examples.ruby: 来月[らいげつ]、京都[きょうと]へ引[ひ]っ越[こ]すつもりです。
examples.english: I'm planning to move to Kyoto next month.

examples.ruby: この話[はなし]はまだ誰[だれ]にも伝[つた]えるつもりはない。
examples.english: I have no intention of passing this on to anyone yet.

examples.ruby: その件[けん]は上司[じょうし]に報告[ほうこく]するつもりだった。
examples.english: I had meant to report that matter to my boss.
